items.title: Firm linked to Jensen Huang's ex-lover reportedly brokered nearly $12 billion in Nvidia chip orders for China
items.desc: Megaspeed, the firm owned by ousted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's former lover Alice Huang, arranged nearly $12 billion in Nvidia chip orders for Chinese companies between 2024 and 2025, according to the WSJ. Short seller Culper Research estimates Nvidia's actual China revenue share exceeds 20 percent, far above the officially reported 7 percent. The article Firm linked to Jensen Huang's ex-lover reportedly brokered nearly $12 billion in Nvidia chip orders for China appeared first on The Decoder .
items.full: Megaspeed arranged nearly $12 billion worth of Nvidia high-performance chip orders for Chinese companies between March 2024 and June 2025, according to documents reviewed by the Wall Street Journal. The company is owned by Alice Huang, the former lover of since-ousted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang . Megaspeed shipped the chips to buyers in China who maintained long-standing business ties with local tech giants, the WSJ reports. The orders covered several hundred thousand chips that the US had sought to keep out of China through export controls. Megaspeed reportedly gained preferential access to scarce AI chips as an Nvidia cloud partner, apparently because it counted Chinese cloud and tech company Alibaba as a major client. Nvidia officially reported $12.4 billion in China revenue over six months, accounting for 7 percent of total revenue. Short-selling firm Culper Research estimates, however, that more than 20 percent of Nvidia's revenue in the last fiscal year came from Chinese customers. A significant share of that China business may have flowed through indirect channels. items.title: Australia's central bank finds AI hitting young workers first, especially in software and customer service
items.desc: Australia's central bank sees early signs that AI is hitting young entry-level workers in highly exposed jobs like software development and customer service. Since ChatGPT launched, job postings and employment among 15- to 24-year-olds in those fields have dropped more sharply than among older workers. Author Mike Major cautions against jumping to conclusions, however, noting that business cycle shifts and remote work trends could also explain the numbers. The article Australia's central bank finds AI hitting young workers first, especially in software and customer service appeared first on Th
items.full: AI has barely displaced any jobs in Australia so far, but young workers entering highly exposed fields like software development are faring worse. An analysis by Mike Major for Australia's central bank (RBA) built a monitoring system that focuses on the areas where effects are likely to appear first, namely entry-level workers and highly AI-exposed occupations such as programming , clerical work, and customer service. According to the analysis , job postings have fallen across all groups since ChatGPT launched in late 2022, with the steepest drop in the highest-exposure group. In that group, workers aged 15 to 24 and young college graduates have weaker employment rates and higher unemployment than older workers. Ad Major cautions against drawing early conclusions, since the study does not establish direct causation and measures only theoretical exposure, not actual use by companies. Post-pandemic shifts in the business cycle or in remote work could also be driving the numbers. According to SEEK data, AI is complementing existing work while also creating new demand for AI skills . Ad An August 2025 Stanford study based on millions of US payroll records found a similar pattern, with employment among 22- to 25-year-olds in AI-exposed occupations down 13 percent in relative terms since late 2022 and nearly 20 percent among young software developers. More experienced workers in the same occupations held steady or gained ground. A March 2026 Anthropic study also found signs of declining hiring among 22- to 25-year-olds in exposed occupations, with job-finding rates down about 14 percent. It found no systematic rise in overall unemployment, however. Theoretical automation potential and actual AI use are far apart, according to the study. Ad Anthropic offers a company-level example. According to an internal review , the share of junior hires in technical roles has fallen from 27 percent to 9 percent since early 2025. In August 2026, AI agents across the company were already logging six times as many hours as human employees. Anthropic concedes that, as an extremely AI-intensive software company, it is a special case. Even so, researchers warn of a "tragedy of the cognitive commons" , in which disappearing junior roles lead to a future shortage of experienced professionals, assuming those professionals are still needed. A large study of 25,000 workers in Denmark confirms the lack of economy-wide impact. Despite a 64 percent AI adoption rate, researchers found no measurable changes in wages or hours worked. Workers saved an average of just 2.8 percent of their working time. Ad A January 2026 analysis of 10.6 million LinkedIn profiles and US unemployment data , however, cautions against blaming the downturn on AI alone. The research team led by Morgan Frank at the University of Pittsburgh found that the problems in exposed occupations started in early 2022, months before ChatGPT launched. Macroeconomic factors like the Fed's shift in interest rate policy or a correction after pandemic-era hiring surges may play a bigger role than previously assumed. items.title: Gemini 4 Carbon takes the MathArena crown but costs 15 times more than GPT-6.1 Sol
items.desc: For the first time in a while, no OpenAI model leads the MathArena AI math benchmark. Google's Gemini 4 Carbon and Anthropic's Fable 5.2 have knocked GPT-6.1 Sol from the top, though both cost significantly more. Gemini ignored the time limit in testing and almost never gave up on a task. The article Gemini 4 Carbon takes the MathArena crown but costs 15 times more than GPT-6.1 Sol appeared first on The Decoder .
items.full: Google's Gemini 4 Carbon has become the first non-OpenAI model in a while to top the MathArena math benchmark. It knocked GPT-6.1 Sol from the top spot, while Claude Fable 5.2 came in second, making it potentially one of the most capable publicly available models for math tasks. OpenAI's models, which recently allegedly solved demanding equations like the Navier-Stokes equations , aren't publicly available yet. Gemini 4 Carbon's most common failure mode is exceeding the time limit. The model also almost never gives up on a task, a trait that can be read as either positive or negative . In one case, it launched a script that ran for more than eleven hours without checking on its progress. That extra performance comes at a price, though. With the reasoning settings used in testing, Carbon and Fable 5.2 cost roughly 15 and 40 times as much as GPT-6.1 Sol, respectively. items.title: OpenAI reassigns robotics researchers to other teams as general-purpose models might make specialized robotics AI unnecessary
items.desc: OpenAI is dissolving its standalone robotics team for the second time, but not because it lacks data. General-purpose models like GPT-6 Astra can apparently control robots directly, making a dedicated unit unnecessary. The researchers are being redistributed across other teams in what the company frames as a way to accelerate its robotics efforts. The article OpenAI reassigns robotics researchers to other teams as general-purpose models might make specialized robotics AI unnecessary appeared first on The Decoder .
items.full: OpenAI is apparently disbanding its robotics team again, but this time for different reasons than in 2020. Rather than abandoning robotics, the company wants to accelerate it by folding researchers into other teams. Robotics researchers are moving to the main research team under Chief Research Officer Mark Chen, while the applied robotics and hardware teams join Greg Brockman's Applied organization. OpenAI made the decision on such short notice that it had already booked a booth at the Conference on Robot Learning (CoRL) in Austin, which then sat empty, Fortune reports . OpenAI apparently believes that general-purpose models like GPT-6 Astra can control robots directly , reducing the need for specialized robotics models. Ad In an Nvidia study , an Astra-powered agent achieved a 74.8 percent success rate on simulated robotics tasks, compared to 51 percent for the best specialized models. The tests used a simulated DROID robot, not a physical one. Ad A new robotics benchmark called StationeryBench compared GPT-6 Astra with Ai2's MolmoAct2 on five tasks involving desk objects on dual-arm YAM robotic arms. Across 200 trials, Astra fully completed 7 out of 100 tasks, while MolmoAct2 didn't complete a single one. Astra's average progress score was 46, compared to 12 for MolmoAct2. In another test, Astra running on a humanoid robot navigated and cleaned up a kitchen. It remains unclear how much robotics data OpenAI and others incorporated during training. Other large general-purpose models from Anthropic and Google have also made recent progress on robotics tasks. Specialized robotics models may still have advantages in cost and reliability as well as speed and energy consumption , even if they don't generalize as well. Ad Yoav Artzi , an AI researcher at Cornell University and Google DeepMind, also sees Astra as a major leap in spatial understanding . On the still-unpublished REMAP benchmark, GPT-6 Astra reaches near-human accuracy, according to Artzi. He suspects that OpenAI may have trained the model on large amounts of 3D training data such as Blender scenes. OpenAI shut down its robotics division in 2020 because, according to co-founder Wojciech Zaremba, the company lacked the training data it needed and large language models were a faster path to AGI. The company rebuilt the team in 2024. CEO Sam Altman is reportedly targeting a first public robot demo for 2027 , and OpenAI wants to build its own everyday robots in the long term. But the company also faces heavy financial pressure to focus on its core AI business , where it has lost significant ground to Anthropic . items.title: Apple launches new app to study how people use AI for health
items.desc: Apple's new app for a study will answer everyday medical questions
items.full: Apple launches new app to study how people use AI for health Ivan Mehta 5:30 PM PST · November 15, 2026 Big AI labs like OpenAI and Anthropic have made their bets on offering chatbots that can answer health-related queries with specialized features. Apple is debuting a new study to understand how people use AI for health. But it isn’t quite following other AI startups just yet; it wants to study how clinically grounded answers can help people. The iPhone maker is partnering with healthcare-focused AI company OpenEvidence to launch a new study app. Apple is inviting users in the U.S. over 21, using iPhone 15 or later, and running iOS 26 or later, with Apple Intelligence enabled. The company is aiming to run this study with up to 200,000 participants for more than 12 months. The new app will allow users to ask health-related questions, as they do with ChatGPT or Claude, with answers grounded in clinical data, from sources including The New England Journal of Medicine, Journal of the American Medical Association, and Nature. Apple said that the app will try to give simplified answers to everyday medical questions. Users can rate those answers and provide feedback about the responses; they’ll also be asked to participate in monthly surveys. Participants can share data from HealthKit such as resting heart rate, activity, sleep, or lab results to get more personalized and pointed suggestions from the app. The company said the app can also help prepare participants better for a doctor’s visit, and it will guide users to specific providers for answers related to concerning medical issues. Apple specified that the data will be anonymized before sending it to a secure third-party cloud provider, and it won’t be used to train any kind of AI models. The company said that OpenEvidence deletes the query and response data after 24 hours. “At Apple, we believe responsible innovation starts with scientific rigor and clinical grounding. Health is deeply personal, and conducting a dedicated research study is the most thoughtful way to understand how people engage with, comprehend, and evaluate health AI in everyday life,” Sumbul Desai, M.D., Apple’s vice president of Health and Fitness, said in a statement, adding, “Insights from this study will help advance the broader scientific conversation and ensure that as technology evolves, we continue building trusted tools that genuinely support people wherever they are on their health journey.” The app is available to download starting today for U.S. users. It’s not clear if Apple wants to release AI-powered answering to its Health app or Siri yet. The potential is huge — earlier this year, OpenAI said users were asking over 300 million health-related queries each week . items.title: I Found A Free Desktop App That Connects Your AI to All Your WordPress Sites
items.desc: Connecting your AI to one WordPress site is easy. Connecting it to thirty client sites across five hosts is where it gets messy. Novamira HQ, now in public beta, gives your AI one connection to all of them, and it's free. The post " I Found A Free Desktop App That Connects Your AI to All Your WordPress Sites " first appeared on WP Mayor .
items.full: Novamira HQ is a free, open source desktop app for macOS, Windows and Linux that gives your AI one connection to every WordPress site you manage. It’s in public beta and the app itself is self-contained, so there’s nothing else to install alongside it, which made me think it’s worth a few minutes of your time. If you’ve used the Novamira plugin , you’ll know how setup has worked until now. Each site gets its own entry in Claude, Cursor, or whichever AI client you use, which is perfectly fine for a couple of sites. But, it gets tedious quick once you’re looking after a list of client sites. If you’re an agency or freelancer, you know you rarely manage just one site. You manage dozens, spread across different hosts, each with its own staging copies. HQ is Novamira’s answer to that, so here’s what the beta includes and how your sites get into it. Novamira HQ sits between your AI client and your WordPress sites, so you connect your AI to HQ once and every site you add to HQ becomes available to it automatically. That includes the sites you add next month, so onboarding a new client just means adding their site to HQ rather than editing the config in every AI tool your team uses. If you’ve already been running Novamira with one entry per site, you can bring those sites into HQ and then remove the old entries from your AI client. Novamira HQ currently supports 13 hosting providers: Kinsta, WP Engine, Hostinger, Cloudways, Pantheon, Pressable, Rocket.net, InstaWP, xCloud, SandyWP, Plesk, cPanel and WHM. When you connect a hosting account, HQ imports every site on it, and depending on what the host allows, you also get environments, backups, and staging-to-production pushes in the same place. If a site doesn’t have the Novamira plugin yet, HQ can install it for you where the host supports it. I’d keep an eye on the cPanel, WHM, and Plesk support in particular, because it brings a lot of traditional and reseller hosting into the picture, not just the managed WordPress hosts. If your client’s site is on a host HQ doesn’t integrate with yet, or it’s sitting on a VPS you look after yourself, you can connect it directly instead. Both kinds of site show up in the same list with their environments and connection status, and your AI works with them in the same way. Novamira HQ has a guided setup for Claude Desktop, Claude Code, ChatGPT, Codex, Cursor, VS Code, and OpenCode, plus a ready-made configuration for Antigravity, and any other MCP-compatible client can connect too. For an agency, that means nobody has to switch tools. Your developer can stick with Cursor or Claude Code while someone on the content side uses Claude Desktop, and they’ll both be working with the same set of sites. HQ works alongside the Novamira plugin, both the free version and Novamira Pro. The plugin is what gives your AI its WordPress abilities on each site, and HQ is what brings all those sites together under one connection. If you want to know more about what the plugin itself can do, our Novamira review goes through it in detail. Novamira HQ keeps your site and hosting credentials on your own computer. There’s no Novamira account to create, no Novamira server sitting in the midd
